newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rain seen helping Brazil's new sugarcane plantings.
newsitem.headline: Rain seen helping Brazil's new sugarcane plantings.

text.p: Forecast rainfall in Brazil's key sugarcane growing regions is likely to benefit new plantings and the second cut but could complicate the harvesting of the current crop in some areas, DataNet-AgriCommodities said.

Heavy showers were expected to persist in the center-south regions of Sao Paulo, Minas Gerais, Goias and Mato Grosso until December 17th and then intensify after December 18th as a cold front moves into the region.
In the producing regions of Parana, around 15 mm of rain was expected between December 16th and 17th.

"The rains forecast for the principal sugarcane areas of the region should have a favorable repercussion on new plantings and the second cut, maintaining a good moisture reserve in soils, but they won't be beneficial to the harvesting conditions of the cane, which is currently in its concluding phase," DataNet said.
It added that rains of between 25 and 100 mm in the key center-south growing regions last week had been mostly beneficial for the next harvest.
In the main growing regions of the north and north-east between Rio Grande do Norte and Alagoas, sunshine will dominate this week although some light showers may fall on isolated coastline areas.
"These should not cause any delays in the harvesting of the 1996/97 crop," DataNet said.

Rainfall was also sparse in the north and northeast last week, with between 10 and 20 mm falling in some coastal areas, linked to sea winds. In the Zona da Mata, rainfall was below 10 mm and benefited new plantings.
